About the Role
 Our client is seeking a Senior AWS DataHub Developer to design and build real-time, event-driven data services on AWS. This role is developer-first (application-side) rather than infrastructure-led. You will architect and deliver Kafka-based streaming pipelines and serverless data applications that ingest, transform, and serve data at scale.
 You’ll collaborate with architects, data engineers, and product teams to deliver secure, resilient, observable, and highly scalable solutions that power enterprise-grade analytics and event-driven applications.
 What You’ll Do (Key Responsibilities)
 Design & Deliver Event-Driven Pipelines: Build serverless data flows using AWS Lambda, Step Functions, EventBridge, SNS, SQS, API Gateway.
 Real-Time Streaming: Develop Kafka (Apache Kafka/Amazon MSK) consumers/producers for high-throughput, low-latency streaming and decoupled microservices.
 Microservices & APIs: Build and optimize TypeScript (preferred) or Python services/APIs for data ingestion, transformation, and delivery.
 AWS Data Services Integration: Work with S3, DynamoDB, Glue, Athena, CloudWatch for storage, metadata, querying, and observability.
 Quality & Reliability: Implement idempotency, retries, dead-letter queues, exactly-once/at-least-once semantics where appropriate, and schema evolution strategies.
 CI/CD & Testing: Use Git-based workflows and CI/CD (e.g., GitHub Actions, Jenkins) with automated tests (unit/integration/load) and infrastructure deployments.
 IaC (Developer View): Define application-layer infrastructure using AWS CDK, Terraform, or CloudFormation—with strong emphasis on developer productivity and repeatability.
 Agile Collaboration: Contribute to technical design, story sizing, peer reviews, and continuous improvement.
 Ideal Candidate Profile
 You are a cloud-native, application-side developer who thinks in events, streams, and services—not servers. You design for resiliency, observability, and scale, and you’re comfortable pairing Kafka with AWS serverless to deliver business outcomes.

Waabi's Commercial Product team defines and delivers the end-to-end commercial product that makes autonomous trucking deployable, scalable, and valuable to customers. We are hiring a Senior Program Manager to own and align the single integrated commercialization plan, ensuring every element converges seamlessly.
While functional program leads manage their respective areas, you will integrate their milestones into the overarching commercial plan. Success relies on sound judgment: identifying critical dependencies, distinguishing real timeline slips, and resolving decision bottlenecks. A year from now, when leadership asks whether we are on track for a launch, a truck delivery or a customer commitment, the answer should be one page, current, and believed by every team on it.
What You'll Do
You will own the integrated commercialization roadmap for trucking and the weekly operating cadence around it. This includes:
Build and own the integrated roadmap that ties customer commitments, OEM truck supply, autonomy and ODD readiness, lane and site activation, Mission Control, operations readiness and Account Management launches to dates, with the dependencies between them made explicit. You own the plan end to end.
Maintain the honest picture: the critical path, the slips, the risks and the decisions needed, surfaced early enough to act on and framed for the people who have to decide.
Lead the execution of key company milestones involving multiple departments at Waabi.
Run the operating cadence, including a weekly cross-functional Truck Program meeting.
Help establish repeatable frameworks, procedures, and decision loops that allow fast and efficient scale.
Produce executive-ready updates and program artifacts.
Communicate clearly with technical, operational, commercial and executive audiences that value first-principles thinking.

Success in this role means the commercial plan converges on purpose rather than by heroics. Specifically, you will have:
Within 90 days, one integrated roadmap that Autonomy, Operations, Sales and Account Management believe, with the Truck Program meeting running off it.
A first driverless launch with no dependency discovered in the final month that was knowable in the first.
Leadership learning about a slip from you, with options, before they learn about it from a customer.
Decisions with a date, an owner and a record, so the same question is not re-decided in three meetings.
Qualifications Required
7+ years in program or product leadership in a complex technical and operational environment (autonomous vehicles, automotive, aerospace, robotics, aviation, defense, logistics or other physical-world deployment).
Track record of integrating programs across teams you did not control, in a business with hardware, software, safety and operations in the loop.
Enough technical fluency to understand why an autonomy or hardware milestone slipped and whether the recovery plan is credible, without needing to be the engineer.
Separates facts, assumptions and risks in how you write and speak; comfortable telling senior people something they do not want to hear, early, with options.
Builds the minimum structure that works and removes or upgrades it when it stops working.
Executive-grade verbal and written communication; most of this role's influence happens in documents and in how a problem is framed.
Set direction for a program others execute, with no direct reports, and being accountable for the outcome anyway.
Strongly Preferred
Ownership mentality: takes initiative and gets into the trenches with key stakeholders.
Varies the degree of detail to the audience and the moment.
Experience running a weekly holistic program review.
Experience taking a physical product from pilot to commercial deployment, where readiness gates and launch dates were real.
Experience working alongside a safety or systems-engineering function on go/no-go decisions.
Experience with OEM or supplier delivery schedules as a dependency in a commercial plan.
Zero-to-one program experience at an early-stage or scaling company.
Nice to have
Direct experience in autonomous trucking, freight or AV commercialization.
Experience working with operations and/or commercial teams.

Hi, I’m Geo, Ashby’s VP of Product. I joined Ashby August ‘26; read more about why I joined here. https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/all/a-letter-from-chris-geoghegan-on-joining-ashby I’m hiring for multiple Product Managers who will report directly to me. More on the specific product areas below.

At Ashby, we have a unique approach to building products https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/culture/ashbys-operating-principles. As a PM, your primary goal is to eliminate frustration and bring delight to our customers. You’ll work with engineers who deeply understand the customer and business problem and own the solution end-to-end. This means that you spend less time writing detailed specs and more time with customers and doing deep product thinking.

Our unique approach is working. We’re growing >100% year over year and have notable customers such as Notion, Linear, OpenAI, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best in class among our peers. We’re backed by amazing investors like Y Combinator, Elad Gil, Lachy Groom, and many more!



PRODUCT AREAS

From day one, we have aimed to build "all-in-one and best-in-class" software for Talent teams. In addition to building a multi-product foundation from day one, we have also focused on enabling customizability and power-user features while keeping Ashby easy to get started with. Doing both is an ambitious undertaking!

We want to continue down this ambitious path in future and add multiple new products, which means we:

 - Are not just building a product, we’re building a platform

 - Need to find a balance between re-usable building blocks and feature-specific behaviour

 - Blend enterprise customizability and ease of use

We also want to continuously delight users. We hear "I never thought one could fall in love with an ATS" quite often, and we want to keep that true for all future products we build.



We are looking for Product Managers who can own the roadmap and strategy for the following areas:

 1. Outbound Sourcing: You’ll build a platform that enables teams to hire sourcing agents directly from Ashby. Customers simply write the job description, and agents start booking calls with highly qualified candidates.
    
    - Great fit if you:
      
      - Love zero-to-one product discovery and turning ambiguous customer problems into new product bets
      
      - Have experience building products that depend on partnerships, integrations, and external ecosystems
      
      - Enjoy balancing user empathy, experimentation, and business impact in a fast-moving space

 2. Product Platform: Ashby was designed from the beginning as a multi-product platform. We’re looking for a PM to establish this team and own the shared building blocks, foundational capabilities, and APIs that let product teams move quickly.
    
    - Great fit if you:
      
      - Bring strong technical product judgment and enjoy working on APIs, shared systems, and foundational capabilities
      
      - Know how to balance reusable building blocks with polished, customer-facing product experiences
      
      - Like creating leverage by helping teams ship quickly and consistently while improving what customers directly see and use

 3. AI Platform: You’ll own the Ashby Assistant, Ashby MCP, and the AI platform used across many product surfaces. You’ll help drive shared primitives, such as AI memory and context.
    
    - Great fit if you:
      
      - Have experience building AI-powered products, especially agents, copilots, or workflow automation
      
      - Enjoy shaping shared AI primitives like memory, context, orchestration, and evaluation
      
      - Can translate fast-moving AI capabilities into products that feel useful, reliable, and delightful

During the interview process, we’ll determine which role you're best suited for. We’re also advertising this opening as Senior Product Manager. Both titles describe the same position; please apply once using the title that best reflects your experience.




YOUR ROLE

 - Drive Impact: Deeply understand our customers and ship impactful product improvements and investments to maintain our strong velocity.

 - Quality: Apply your strong product taste and sound judgement to deliver solutions that are both powerful and a joy to use. Use your judgment to identify areas where we need to improve quality before shipping.

 - Prioritization and Strategy: Maintain a roadmap to ensure engineering is never blocked, and set a compelling strategy and vision for the next 6-18 months.

 - Customer Research: Spend time with customers and customer-facing teams. Synthesize customer feedback, research, and competitive intel to drive smart prioritization choices.

 - Execution Excellence: Set the pace for your product area by identifying bottlenecks, scoping effectively, and driving projects toward high-impact releases. Stay close to engineering work to navigate tradeoffs, manage technical risks, and resolve execution challenges.

 - Cross-functional Collaboration: Partner across go-to-market teams to bring the features and products your team builds to the market. Anticipate and plan for the needs to help inform pricing, marketing, and customer support.

 - Ownership and reliability: follow through on commitments, manage time ruthlessly, respond promptly to stakeholders, and communicate proactively when priorities or timelines change.




YOU COULD BE A GREAT FIT IF

 - You have an unnatural curiosity and excitement about the end-user and the jobs they do

 - You bring an Engineering mindset to product problems and can think through edge cases and understand how to extend our underlying platform to create leverage

 - You can demonstrate taste - you care about the quality of the products you build and use

 - You're an excellent writer and synthesizer; you bring product knowledge and clarity to the entire organization and enable Engineers with product insights

 - You can build a thesis for prioritization and communicate priorities using a sound strategy that combines principled thinking, research, and data

 - You leverage tools and processes to build operational excellence into your product process

 - You have a strong business sense and understand how product and GTM should collaborate, how your features may be monetized, and how product priorities fit into larger business priorities




YOU MAY NOT BE A GREAT FIT IF

 - You prefer to specify exactly what Engineering should build rather than give engineers room to own the solution.

 - You dislike written documentation and prefer to manage the team via meetings and quick Slack messages.

 - You’re primarily interested in shipping features and not thinking through how to make them reusable platform capabilities.

 - You don’t enjoy doing deep research yourself and prefer to outsource that UX research, market research, and data teams.

 - You’re uncomfortable moving with urgency, making tradeoffs, and reprioritizing when new information emerges.

 - You’re primarily motivated by achieving a metric more than delivering a great product experience for customers.




WE WORK DIFFERENTLY

At Ashby, the role of Product Managers is different from what I’ve seen in most product orgs. At a high level, PMs are responsible for shipping impactful product changes at high velocity, consistently and over an extended period. When we think about impactful product changes, our primary goal is to remove frustration and add delight.

At many organizations, PMs are required to write detailed specs that handle every edge case. Designers are required to mock up every pixel. At Ashby, it’s different. We believe individual contributors do their best work when they have a deep understanding of the end user and the business, and ownership of the solution. This is reflected in the engineers Ashby hires: they own projects end-to-end and deeply understand the problems they are solving. PMs are expected to give significant white space in their specs. As a result, PMs can spend less time managing tickets and more time with customers and thinking deeply about the product strategy.

At Ashby, PMs need to be the pace-setters for their product areas. This means they bring a healthy level of impatience and time-paranoia to the table. This does not mean cutting corners or demanding that engineers work unreasonable hours. As a PM, you can help engineers by managing the project scope well, identifying when it’s appropriate to bring in help, or being ruthless about prioritization.

For PM roles at Ashby, we believe great products are built through deep thinking and a clear understanding of user needs. A major part of your role involves conducting thorough user research to uncover underlying customer problems and translating those insights into well-reasoned product strategies.

Finally, Ashby isn’t simply an ATS. Right from the foundations, it was designed to be much more than that. It’s a platform modelled around how organizations (from early-stage startups to massive enterprises) think about recruiting, managing, and retaining top talent. As a PM at Ashby, you should, over time, get familiar with our most common building blocks. You’ll invest not only in product improvements but in platform thinking.




INTERVIEW PROCESS

If this also sounds exciting to you, please apply. We review every application and aim to get back to candidates within 2-3 days. For candidates that advance to the interview process, here is what you can expect:

 1. Intro Call - 30 mins

 2. Product Experience Deep Dive - 1 hour

 3. Product Exercise - 1 hour

 4. Final Round Interview - 2 hours
    Mostly focused on cross-functional Interviews to meet more of the team. This is a critical hire for us and a role that will touch a lot of functions - we want to make sure you'll meet folks you'll be working closely with.




BENEFITS

 - 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

 - Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year.

 - Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise.

 - Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

 - $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

 - $250/month tool budget plus access to Claude, Cursor, and Codex with generous token budgets.

 - If you’re in the US, we offer top-tier health insurance for you and your dependents, with 100% of premiums covered by Ashby. In other countries, we provide high-quality supplemental health insurance for you and your dependents, which is also fully covered by us.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

Supporting growth, development, and driving performance is where this role comes in.

Reporting into the Manager, Key Account Management, as a Key Account Manager you will own the long-term partnership with Jobber's largest customers. While inbound sales and onboarding create the initial relationship, you take it from there: driving retention, growing payment processing volume (GPV), and expanding the value customers get from Jobber over time.

You'll act as a trusted business advisor, helping clients achieve their goals and maximize their ROI on Jobber and you'll do it with confidence, curiosity, and authenticity. You bring real expertise from working with many similar businesses, while staying genuinely curious about each SP's specific situation and tailoring your approach accordingly.

This was a new department at Jobber! One that's been proven to be successful over the past couple of years. We're looking for people who are excited by the opportunity to leave their mark on a massive revenue opportunity for the company, while also growing their own skills and career.



Please note: This role is only eligible to candidates in either Vancouver, Toronto, Edmonton or Kitchener-Waterloo 


As a Key Account Manager you will:

 - Manage a portfolio of ~300 high-value accounts, focused on three core outcomes: retaining customers and preventing churn, growing Gross Payment Volume (the dollar amount processed through Jobber Payments), and upselling plan upgrades and add-ons that create real value

 - Drive GPV growth across your portfolio by identifying value opportunities for clients to process more through Jobber Payments

 - Build deep, consultative relationships with key clients - acting as a strategic partner, not just a point of contact

 - Conduct regular business reviews and strategic planning sessions with key clients, providing insights and recommendations on how to optimize their use of Jobber's products and services, particularly those related to payments

 - Guide customers to take action, bringing a bias toward live problem-solving on calls

 - Identify and drive upsell and cross-sell opportunities, with a focus on expansion and increasing customer lifetime value

 - Increase the gross payment volume of your assigned accounts, as well as the overall customer lifetime value as well as cross sell other potential Jobber products

 - Develop and implement best practices and processes for the Key Account Management department, as well as mentor and coach other team members

 - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills

 - Ability to work independently and as part of a team

 - Client-focused consultative mindset

 - Proficiency with the challenger sales methodology

 - Familiarity with Jobber's products and services

 - Experience working with or in the home services industry (Nice To Have)

Perplexity innovates at the frontier of AI infrastructure, search, and orchestration to serve the world's most discerning users. The Perplexity API Platform brings our technology to the world's most discerning developers. From exabyte-scale knowledge indexes to codegen-first agent runtimes, the building blocks behind Perplexity's applications are some of the most battle-tested AI systems in the industry.

We believe these same building blocks can and should power the aspirations of builders everywhere. It's one thing to solve planet-scale retrieval, long-horizon orchestration, and other foundational AI challenges within a single product ecosystem. The true measure of success is to turn those solutions into elegant APIs that delight developers and agents alike. Our API Platform delivers frontier intelligence to thousands of customers: startups, trillion-dollar enterprises, U.S. and allied governments, and everyone in between.

We've achieved incredible scale, yet we're just getting started. Join us to build tools for curious minds.




ABOUT THIS ROLE

Perplexity is seeking strong engineers with a passion for delivering frontier intelligence and infrastructure to developers. Our company builds technology that reshapes how people search, reason, and interact with the world around them. Week after week, we observe increasing demand for programmatic interfaces to that technology. The API Platform engineering team is charged with designing, implementing, and scaling these interfaces.

As a member of our team, you'll work on an eclectic portfolio spanning distributed systems, performance optimization, agent orchestration, and frontier topics that often change with each passing month. Throughout this work, you'll prioritize great developer and agent experience alike. You'll also define technical strategy for how we scale to meet compounding growth exponentials (number of customers, agents per customer, compute/retrieval per agent, etc.).

 - Design, build, and operate mission-critical APIs that provide our customers the building blocks for frontier intelligence.

 - Own and evolve the API gateway and routing layer: authentication, authorization, rate limiting and quotas, usage metering, and request routing across heterogeneous upstream services.

 - Build API governance into the platform: contract-first schemas, breaking-change detection in CI, versioning and deprecation workflows, and SDKs and documentation generated from a single source of truth.

 - Unify cross-cutting capabilities (billing and usage, rate limiting, organization and identity settings, analytics and observability) so every API product gets them by default instead of rebuilding them.

 - Ensure low latency and high throughput through aggressive performance optimization (including on upstream systems).

 - Harden system security and reliability across heterogeneous compute environments, and operate what you build: SLOs, on-call, and incident response.

 - Collaborate across teams to bring novel frontier capabilities into the API Platform, and partner with infrastructure teams on compute, networking, secrets, and security.

 - Continually reimagine the customer needs of tomorrow (and the architectures to serve those needs), while faithfully serving the customer workloads of today.

 - Uphold engineering excellence through design reviews, code quality, and internal documentation.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - 5+ years of backend engineering experience with Python, Go, or Rust, including significant time building platforms or infrastructure used by other engineering teams.

 - Strong understanding of high-traffic API design: schema evolution & versioning, idempotency, authentication patterns, rate limiting, and performance tuning.

 - Experience building API governance tooling: contract-first API design, breaking-change detection and API linting in CI, versioning and deprecation workflows, and SDKs and documentation generated from the contract.

 - Platform depth across the build and deploy path: you have owned CI/CD pipelines, container builds and base images, infrastructure as code, and progressive delivery (canary or blue-green) on a major cloud.

 - A track record of owning a platform end to end: identifying the need, designing it, aligning the teams that depend on it, shipping it, and operating it, while raising the engineering bar for the teams building on it.

Strong plus:

 - Experience with modern AI APIs (including latency tuning, streaming, model orchestration, emerging technical standards).

 - Usage-based billing and metering systems, multi-tenant organization and identity models, and usage analytics pipelines.

 - Observability for API platforms: structured logging pipelines, metrics, tracing, and SLO tooling.

 Win new restaurants, from first visit to signed agreement

You'll sit down with owners and general managers in their restaurants to learn how the phone is handled today: who answers it, what gets missed during service, and what those missed calls cost in bookings and orders. Then you'll demo Sadie against that picture.
 You'll scope what the restaurant needs, write the proposal, negotiate terms and get the agreement signed. 
 Most of the judgement is in qualification. A good demo with someone who can't sign, or a restaurant Sadie can't serve yet, costs you weeks. You're expected to spot that early and move on.
 Build your own pipeline across your territory 
 You'll generate your own leads through outbound outreach, networking and on-site visits. That means planning which neighbourhoods and restaurant groups to work, walking in at the right time of day, and following up until you get a meeting.
 Hit your targets with a forecast you can defend 
 You're measured against monthly and quarterly sales targets, and the expectation is that you hit them consistently. You'll keep every opportunity accurate in HubSpot, so that stage, value and close date mean something to the people who plan around them.
 Represent Sadie where restaurant people meet 
 You'll attend local industry events, restaurant meetups and trade shows across your geography. You'll decide which ones are worth the evening, run the conversations there, and turn them into meetings within the week.
 For a lot of operators, you'll be the first person from Sadie they meet. What they hear from you is what they'll repeat to other owners.
 Hand over accounts that go live well 
 The restaurant buys Sadie, but the guest ringing to book a table decides whether it works. You'll give onboarding and customer success a written record of what you promised, what the owner expects, and what could go wrong.
 If you oversell, the owner finds out on a Friday night and the guest pays for it. Set expectations you can stand behind.
 What you'll bring
 At least 2 years in a closing sales role, selling software or services to businesses.
 A record of meeting targets, and the ability to explain how you did it.
 Experience running the whole cycle yourself, from prospecting through to signature.
 Comfort with in-person selling, including cold visits and demos in front of a busy owner.
 Strong discovery skills. You can find out what an operator needs in fifteen minutes between services.
 Clear written communication. Your proposals and follow-ups are accurate and short.
 An honest forecast. You'd rather call a deal lost than carry it for another month.
 You use AI every day for research, preparation and drafting, and you check what it produces.
 You organise your own week across a territory and follow through without being managed.
 Useful experience
 Selling to restaurants or other hospitality operators.
 Working in a restaurant yourself, front of house or in management.
 Selling reservations, POS, telephony or other restaurant technology.
 An existing network among restaurant owners in your territory.
 Selling AI products to non-technical buyers.
 Being an early sales hire at a startup.
 Who will enjoy this role
 You like finding out how a business really works. When an owner says they miss calls at seven on a Saturday, you want to know how many, what those calls were for, and what happened to the guest who hung up.
 In a single week you might walk into six restaurants before lunch service, run a demo at a bar between shifts, spend an evening at a trade show, and sit with onboarding to sort out an account you signed. Your schedule follows the restaurant day, and some of your best conversations will happen at three in the afternoon or late at night.
 The hard parts are specific. Owners are busy and sceptical, and many will turn you away mid-service. You'll hear no far more often than yes, and you'll still need to be back through the next door the same afternoon. Some of the material you'd expect to have, such as local case studies or a settled playbook, may not exist yet, and you'll help build it while carrying a number.
 Why this role matters
 Sadie is building technology for hospitality. Restaurants lose revenue to calls nobody picks up, and our product exists to answer them.
 This role is how Sadie reaches the restaurants in your geography. You decide who to visit and how each customer starts. The agreements you sign affect revenue, what onboarding and customer success inherit, and what a guest hears when they ring to book a table.
 You'll own new restaurant business across your territory, with the authority to decide how Sadie wins it.

Who we are 
 About Stripe 
 Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.
 About the team 
 In this role, you will be joining the High Availability and Disaster Recovery team. At Stripe, availability is a core feature of our products. This team designs and builds new solutions to allow latency-critical, stateful applications to survive any type of disaster. We build distributed systems on top of unreliable architecture to provide highly available and resilient customer solutions. This team is creating greenfield solutions which will serve as the basis for Stripe’s architecture 5, 10, or 20 years into the future.
 This is a distributed team with many remote engineers. You are encouraged to apply if you meet the minimum requirements and are able to work from anywhere in the United States or Canada.
 What you’ll do 
 You will help develop our global architecture by combining less-available components and data centers into a highly available and resilient whole. You will work on latency-critical solutions where every millisecond matters and data redundancy is a hard requirement. You will learn quickly and work on a broad range of problems - one day may be investigating Mongo write concerns, the next may be minimizing cross-region TLS handshakes, followed by developing new systems to automate disaster detection and failovers. Your work will enable Stripe to increase the GDP of the internet by providing uptime and data protection which have historically been impossible.
 Responsibilities 
 Actively work with leaders and engineers across the company to understand and identify opportunities to improve Stripe’s reliability posture
 Scope, design, implement, and deploy robust distributed services, making appropriate tradeoffs between reliability, throughput, latency, resiliency, engineering velocity and cost
 Innovate, design and implement new products and prototypes to improve service resiliency, engineering velocity and management at scale
 Mentor and grow the next generation of technical leaders at Stripe
 Contribute to engineering strategy, tooling, processes, and culture
 Uphold our high engineering standards and improve our codebase and processes
 Who you are 
 We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
 Minimum requirements 
 Have 10 years or more of distributed and cloud native software development experience at a highly-scaled or hyperscaler service
 Have a deep understanding of how to build scalable, resilient, distributed systems, cloud native architectures, and mission critical systems.
 Have experience influencing, planning, scoping, and leading large projects across many teams
 Thrive in a collaborative environment involving diverse stakeholders and subject matter experts
 Have a high level of autonomy and responsibility, and think of yourself as entrepreneurial, proactive and self-driven
 Have a strong history of being a technical lead and mentor across several engineering teams

ABOUT THE ROLE 
 LEAP is hiring a Social Media Manager to bring our brand, products, and services to life through compelling social storytelling that builds brand awareness, grows our audience, and drives customer acquisition. The candidate will own social strategy recommendations, content planning, day-to-day channel execution, reporting—and employ a journalistic mindset while producing content onsite with clients and internal stakeholders. 
 Reporting to the CEO and Director of Marketing, you will take a hands-on role in executing our social media strategy, developing content plans and editorial calendars aligned with business objectives, product launches, and industry events. The Director of Marketing and CEO will drive business priorities, campaign goals and budget approvals; while the internal marketing team will own overall brand direction.
 You will create and publish engaging, platform-specific content, experiment with creative approaches, and use performance insights to continuously optimize campaigns. Beyond creating content, you will connect social media activity to measurable business outcomes, tracking audience growth, engagement, website traffic, lead generation, and customer acquisition. Working closely with internal stakeholders, you will build a strong understanding of LEAP’s products, services, and the Canadian legal industry, while capturing authentic client stories and industry buzz at events and on-site visits. 
 This is a one-year opportunity for a creative, results-driven social media professional to accelerate LEAP’s digital presence, demonstrate measurable marketing impact, and help shape the future of our social media program. This is a full-time, one year contract position. 
 ***This role is hybrid, requiring 3 days per week in our downtown Toronto office*** 
 About LEAP 
 LEAP leads the world in cloud-based legal practice management software. Our curiosity and commitment to continual improvement have kept us reimagining productivity tools for lawyers and their staff to support our guiding purpose, which is to ‘Help lawyers who help people.’ The market-leading software we develop, and support is used by more than 100,000 lawyers and their staff in small and medium-sized law firms.
 Working alongside our international team of passionate high achievers, you’ll join a fast-growing technology business where things seldom stay the same for long. With more than 1000 smart, caring and ambitious ‘LEAPsters’ working together across Australia, Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, the Republic of Ireland, Poland and New Zealand, you’ll be in good company here.
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND ACCOUNTABILITIES 
 Own social strategy recommendations, content planning, day-to-day channel execution, reporting while producing content onsite with clients and internal stakeholders.
 Develop and refine social media narratives that support brand awareness and customer acquisition goals 
 Build content plans and editorial calendars aligned to business priorities, product launches, and events 
 Create, adapt, and publish social content across agreed channels in partnership with the internal marketing team 
 Translate campaign themes into channel-specific storytelling that fits audience behavior and platform best practices 
 Run structured testing on messaging, creative angles, formats, timing, and CTAs 
 Monitor performance and recommend changes based on engagement, audience growth, traffic, lead volume and quality, and conversion signals 
 Partner with internal stakeholders to gather inputs, approvals, and campaign/messaging context 
 Travel to events and locations in order to capture client engagement and “industry buzz”  
 Identify opportunities to improve reach, consistency, and efficiency across the social program 
 Deliver regular reporting that connects social activity to marketing outcomes, especially customer acquisition 
 Maintain an organized workflow for planning, production, publishing, and performance review 
 Continually remain engaged with internal stakeholders to learn about our product and service workflows, and the legal industry in Canada 
 Up to approximately 20% of travel required to client sites located within Canada
 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 
 5 years of experience in a similar role
 Convey a confident, energetic and professional demeanor with clear and authentic tone 
 Proven freelance or in-house experience managing social media for an established brand 
 Strong background in strategic storytelling and campaign execution across social channels 
 Identify and extract viral trends and capitalize on those opportunities to get more visibility 
 Experience building content calendars, workback schedules while managing multiple workstreams with deadlines in Trello 
 Ability to use performance data to guide testing, iteration, and content decisions with a focus on business outcomes 
 Expert hands-on skills using Hootsuite, Bitly, Meta, LinkedIn, YouTube and X 
 Track video-to-lead journeys, measure engagement and conversions, and isolate video campaign performance from other marketing efforts 
 Clear understanding of audience growth tactics and social content optimization 
 Strong writing and editing skills with the ability to adapt tone and messaging by channel and key message instance 
 Hands-on skills curating video assets using editing tools such as CapCut, Canva, Jitter 
 Basic graphic design skills using Canva with a well-appointed eye for typesetting 
 Ability to adapt social content designs to existing LEAP brand guidelines and adjust designs according to feedback 
 Ability to work independently to achieve KPIs while aligning with internal stakeholders for IP and feedback

WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

Business Need

We are overhauling our Salesforce system, which will require significant updates to the data models and pipelines that support revenue reporting. We also lack scalable visibility into self-serve revenue due to fragmented data sources and manual reporting processes. This role will help build and maintain the data infrastructure and automated reporting needed to support these changes and improve visibility across go-to-market and finance teams.

Role Description

This intern will support Revenue Operations data infrastructure and automation, including data enrichment and management, building and updating data pipelines, and developing automated reporting for go-to-market and finance stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

 - Support go-to-market reporting, systems, and processes that help teams make data-driven decisions and drive revenue growth.

 - Help maintain and improve data quality across Salesforce and other go-to-market systems.

 - Work with cross-functional teams to bring together customer data across product usage, sales activity, marketing engagement, support, and contract data.

 - Support the development and maintenance of dashboards and reporting for go-to-market and finance leadership.

 - Assist with data pipelines and processes that connect data across Salesforce, BigQuery, and other systems.

 - Help identify opportunities to automate manual reporting and operational processes.

 - Support ad hoc data analysis and operational requests from the Revenue team.

What You Bring

 - Interest in learning about Revenue Operations, data analytics, and how technology companies go to market.

 - Some experience working with data through coursework, internships, projects, or extracurricular activities.

 - Comfort with spreadsheets and a willingness to develop skills in tools such as SQL, Salesforce, BigQuery, Looker, or Tableau.

 - Strong problem-solving ability and an enjoyment of figuring out how data, systems, and processes fit together.

 - Detail orientation and a commitment to data accuracy and quality.

 - Comfort with learning new tools and working across multiple projects.

 - Ability to communicate findings clearly and explain what the data means and why it matters.

Position Details

Duration: 4 months

Start date: January 4

Location: Toronto or New York

ABOUT FLOAT

Float is on a mission to simplify finance for Canadian businesses, empowering them to eliminate complexity and unlock new opportunities. Through our innovative platform, Float enables businesses to streamline financial operations and optimize cash flow, so they can focus on what matters most: growth. 

 

As one of Canada’s fastest growing companies https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/rob-magazine/top-growing-companies/article-ranking-canadas-top-growing-companies-of-2024/ and top-rated startups in 2025 https://www.linkedin.com/posts/floatfinancial_were-proud-to-share-that-float-has-been-activity-7387093684720300032-2DDz/, 2024 https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/linkedin-top-startups-2024-15-canadian-companies-rise-linkedin-news-llihe/ and 2023 https://lnkd.in/TSU23CA, Float is customer-obsessed, passionate and entrepreneurial, with a team that includes leaders from Uber, Stripe, Shopify, Top Hat, Ada, Doordash, Snowflake, and Wealthsimple.

 

At Float, everyone is an owner, bringing their unique perspective to our team and product. Your voice is important, and we take having a culture based on feedback seriously. We openly share our thoughts and differing opinions so we can continue to improve. We do our best to keep our decision-making decentralized so that all team members feel ownership in our success.

 


OUR PRODUCT

Float is Canada’s intelligent financial operating system, combining modern financial services and software to help businesses spend, save, and grow. Trusted by more than 10,000 Canadian companies, Float provides high-limit corporate cards, automated expense management, next-day bill payments, high-yield accounts, and industry-leading support, all built in Canada, for Canada. Float recently announced our $85 million Series C https://floatfinancial.com/press/float-financial-raises-cad-85-million-series-c, and is backed by world-class investors, including Inovia Capital, Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, OMERS Ventures, and Silicon Valley Bank.

 

Our team is a collection of ambitious, collaborative and mission-driven people from all walks of life but with one goal: helping Canadian companies not just survive but thrive. And we’re looking for bold innovators to help shape the future of business finance in Canada.




AI USE IN OUR HIRING PROCESS

We use technology, including artificial intelligence (AI), to support parts of our hiring process. This may include AI-assisted scheduling and candidate communications, and AI-generated interview notes, guides or summaries to help our team focus on the conversation. All hiring decisions are made by our hiring team.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Customer Success Manager, you’ll play a critical role in ensuring our customers successfully adopt and maximize the value of Float from the moment they onboard and throughout their journey. You’ll be a trusted partner, working closely with customers to drive strong adoption, mitigate risks, and unlock long-term growth opportunities.



At Float, we believe great customer success is about building meaningful partnerships and unlocking long-term value for our customers. If you’re passionate about driving adoption, mitigating risks, and helping businesses scale their financial operations, we’d love to hear from you!




WHAT YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR


BUILDING AN EARLY FOUNDATION FOR LONG-TERM SUCCESS

 - Build deep relationships with customers as they begin their Float journey, ensuring a smooth and successful onboarding experience.

 - Partner with key stakeholders to define success criteria and measurable outcomes for their initial adoption of Float.

 - Identify long-term expansion opportunities by deeply understanding each customer’s broader financial operations and future needs.

 - Ensure customers stay on track with their year-one objectives, including spend targets and product adoption milestones.

 - Serve as a strategic partner post-onboarding to drive continued engagement, training, and advocacy within customer organizations.

 - Proactively monitor customer health signals and usage patterns, ensuring any barriers to adoption are addressed early.


PROACTIVELY MANAGING RISK AND RETENTION

 - Identify risks across your book of business and develop proactive mitigation plans in partnership with cross-functional teams.

 - Ensure customers remain engaged and see ongoing value from Float by addressing potential churn indicators before they escalate.

 - Support customers through any transitions, ensuring they continue to leverage Float’s full capabilities.


CHAMPIONING PRODUCT ADOPTION & DRIVING INNOVATION

 - Drive customer adoption of Float’s full suite of features, ensuring teams maximize the value of corporate and employee spend management.

 - Advocate for customer participation in Float’s Early Adopter Programs, gathering insights to shape future product iterations.

 - Educate and inspire customers to explore new ways to optimize their workflows with Float’s evolving capabilities.

 - Identify opportunities for growth across your aligned Book of Business. 


BEING THE VOICE OF THE CUSTOMER AT FLOAT

 - Provide insight and strategic recommendations on how Float can best serve our customers, from social proof to feature enhancements.

 - Partner with internal teams to leverage customer feedback for product development and operational improvements.

 - Help accelerate learning cycles by engaging customers who share our passion for simplifying corporate spending.

 - Collaborate on initiatives that impact Float’s customers, from onboarding programs to strategic campaigns that drive engagement and growth.

 - Support the development and execution of scalable processes that enhance the customer experience at every stage of their journey.




ABOUT YOU


HERE’S WHAT SETS YOU UP FOR SUCCESS AT FLOAT:

 - You Put Customers First, Always. You care deeply about delivering meaningful value. Whether you're building internal systems or customer-facing features, you're always thinking about how to make life better for our users.

 - You Act Like an Owner. You take responsibility for outcomes, step up to challenges, and seek solutions proactively—doing what’s best for the business, not just your role.

 - You Think Big and Move Fast. You’re energized by building from 0 to 1. You’re not afraid to challenge the status quo, experiment quickly, and learn as you go.

 - You Constantly Learn and Grow. You’re hungry to improve your craft and open to feedback. You bring a growth mindset to everything you do.

 - You Raise the Bar. You care about doing things well and efficiently. You balance speed with rigor and always look for ways to improve how we work.

 - You Win as a Team. You’re a generous collaborator who values communication, context, and shared wins. You lift others up and help make the team stronger.




IN ADDITION TO LIVING OUR VALUES...

You have a proven track record of driving product adoption, retention, and expansion within a B2B customer-base. 
   
   - Nice to have: 
     
     - CPA, CA, CFA designation

You actively contribute to internal initiatives, such as playbook development, process improvements, or customer advocacy programs, to scale impact beyond your own book of business.
